blocks.text: (RA) said, "It was this that you had intended asking from the outset! Whenever I asked (Rasulullaah ﷺ) anything, I would receive a reply and whenever I remained silent, I would be informed." [^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Concerning the Knowledge of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) is certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef (one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He is (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen." The narrator says, "I thought that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) had perhaps made an error because Allaah says in the Qur'aan:

blocks.arabic_text: اِنَّ اِبْرٰهِيْمَ كَانَ اُمَّةً قَانِتًا لِّلّٰهِ حَنِيْفًا ۭ وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِيْنَ شَاكِرًا لِّاَنْعُمِهٖ ۭ اِجْتَبٰىهُ وَهَدٰىهُ اِلٰى صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيْمٍ
blocks.text: Ibraheem (AS) was certainly an Ummah who was Qaanit and Haneef (one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds). He was (definitely) not from the Mushrikeen.

However, when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) repeated his words to me, I knew that he meant what he was saying. I therefore remained silent. He then asked, 'Do you know what the meaning of 'Ummah' and 'Qaanit' is?' When I submitted that Allaah knows best, he explained, 'Ummah (in this context) refers to a person who teaches people good things and 'Qaanit' refers to a person who obeys Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. That is exactly how Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was. He taught people everything that was good and was obedient to Allaah and to Allaah's Rasool ﷺ.'" [^2]
Statements of Hadhrat Masrooq Concerning the Knowledge of the Sahabah (RA)

Hadhrat Masrooq says, "I examined the Sahabah (RA) carefully and found that all their knowledge could be found in six of them; namely Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA). After closely examining these six, I discovered that all their knowledge could be found in Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)." [^3]
Hadhrat Masrooq also said, "When I arrived in Madinah and enquired about the Sahabah (RA), I discovered that amongst those with the most profound knowledge was Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA)." [^4]
